target: Je me suis fait avoir par un escroc.
english: I got scammed by a con artist.
tip: 'Se faire avoir' is literally 'to get oneself had' – the set phrase for being tricked or scammed: 'je me suis fait avoir' = I got taken in, I fell for it.

target: Avant qu'il ne parte, je veux lui parler.
english: Before he leaves, I want to speak to him.
tip: 'Avant que' + ne expletif (optional): 'avant qu'il ne parte'. The 'ne' has no negative meaning here.

target: Il a raconté qu'il avait failli avoir un accident.
english: He told that he had almost had an accident.
tip: 'Faillir' + verb means to nearly do something: 'avait failli avoir un accident' = had almost had a crash. This verb basically only lives in past tenses.

target: Bien que le temps fût mauvais, le voyage était merveilleux.
english: Although the weather was bad, the trip was wonderful.
tip: 'Bien que' (although) always forces the subjunctive: 'bien que le temps fût'. That 'fût' is the literary imperfect subjunctive of être – in speech you'd just say 'soit'.

target: Il a fait construire une maison à la campagne.
english: He had a house built in the countryside.
tip: 'Faire' + infinitive = causative: 'faire construire' = to have built. The subject causes the action.

target: Ça craint, ce resto.
english: This restaurant sucks.
tip: Very informal: 'ça craint' = that sucks. Slang, never use in formal contexts.

target: Il m'a posé un lapin hier.
english: He stood me up yesterday.
tip: Poser un lapin is literally 'to place a rabbit', but it means to stand someone up. Il m'a posé un lapin = he no-showed and left me waiting. No rabbit involved.

target: Je ne crois pas qu'il ait raison.
english: I don't think he's right.
tip: Negative belief triggers subjunctive: ne pas croire que + subj.

target: Il s'est fait la malle sans prévenir personne.
english: He ran off without telling anyone.
tip: 'se faire la malle' literally means 'pack your trunk' – slang for clearing off suddenly: 'il s'est fait la malle' = he ran off.

target: Mon collègue m'a demandé ce que je pensais du projet.
english: My colleague asked me what I thought of the project.
tip: Reported speech: 'Qu'est-ce que tu penses?' → 'ce que je pensais'.

target: T'inquiète, c'est pas grave.
english: Don't worry, it's no big deal.
tip: Familier: 'T'inquiète' = 'Ne t'inquiète pas'. Dropped 'ne' is typical.

target: Il a insisté pour que nous partions immédiatement.
english: He insisted that we leave immediately.
tip: 'insister' needs 'pour' before 'que', where English expects a plain 'that': 'insister pour que nous partions' – and 'partions' is subjunctive.

target: Que ce soit clair, je n'accepterai aucun compromis.
english: Make no mistake, I will accept no compromise.
tip: 'Que ce soit clair' = 'let it be clear.' A sentence-starting Que + subjunctive (soit) fires off a wish or order, where English reaches for 'let' or 'may.'

target: Il a trop la classe avec son nouveau costard.
english: He looks so cool in his new suit.
tip: Familier: 'avoir la classe' = 'to look cool', 'costard' = 'costume/suit'.

target: Votre concours nous est précieux et nous vous en remercions.
english: Your support is precious to us and we thank you for it.
tip: 'Concours' normally means a competition or contest – but in formal French it means help or support. 'Votre concours' here is your assistance, not a contest.

target: Ce n'est pas tant le prix qui me gêne que le manque de qualité.
english: It's not so much the price that bothers me as the lack of quality.
tip: 'Ce n'est pas tant...que': 'it's not so much...as'.

target: Il fait un froid de canard.
english: It's bitterly cold.
tip: 'Un froid de canard' = 'bitter cold'. Origin: duck hunting in winter.

target: Il semble que ce soit vrai.
english: It seems that it's true.
tip: Il semble que + subjunctive (uncertainty). Il me semble que + indicative (more certain).

target: Ménager la chèvre et le chou.
english: To try to please everyone.
tip: 'Ménager la chèvre et le chou' is literally 'spare the goat and the cabbage' – feed the goat without letting it eat the cabbage. Means please both sides.

target: C'est le plus beau paysage que j'aie jamais vu.
english: It's the most beautiful landscape I've ever seen.
tip: After a superlative, French switches to the subjunctive: 'le plus beau... que j'aie jamais vu' takes aie, not ai. Same after seul, premier, dernier.

target: Tourner autour du pot.
english: To beat around the bush.
tip: Literally 'circling around the pot,' where English beats around the bush – both mean stalling instead of getting to the point.

target: Mettre son grain de sel.
english: To put in one's two cents.
tip: 'Mettre son grain de sel' is literally 'to add your grain of salt' – but it means butting in with an unasked opinion, not the English skepticism sense.

target: Quoi que vous fassiez, restez calme.
english: Whatever you do, stay calm.
tip: 'Quoi que' (two words) + subjunctive = whatever. Don't confuse with 'quoique' (one word) = although.

target: Crois-tu qu'il soit capable de le faire ?
english: Do you think he's capable of doing it?
tip: Interrogative croire que can trigger subjunctive when doubt is implied.

target: Il est dommage que tu ne puisses pas venir.
english: It's a shame you can't come.
tip: 'Il est dommage que' + subjunctive: regret/judgment triggers subjunctive.

target: Il est peu probable qu'il accepte.
english: It's unlikely he'll accept.
tip: 'Il est peu probable que' + subjunctive: low probability triggers subjunctive.

target: Tout brillant qu'il soit, il manque d'expérience.
english: Brilliant though he is, he lacks experience.
tip: 'Tout brillant qu'il soit' = 'however brilliant he may be.' Tout + adjective + que takes the subjunctive (soit) to concede a point.

target: Nous avons le plaisir de vous informer que votre demande a été acceptée.
english: We are pleased to inform you that your request has been accepted.
tip: 'Nous avons le plaisir de' = we are pleased to. Standard business/formal announcement opening.

target: Avoir un pied-à-terre.
english: To have a small apartment to stay in.
tip: 'Pied-à-terre' = a second home, usually small, in another city.

target: Grave, je suis d'accord avec toi.
english: Totally, I agree with you.
tip: Familier: 'grave' alone = 'totally/absolutely'. Youth slang.
